description: ERA5 is the fifth generation ECMWF reanalysis of global weather and climate, which combines model data with observations from across the world by data assimilation into a complete and consistent record. It contains hourly estimates of many atmospheric, ocean-wave and land-surface quantities, such as near-surface temperature and wind, precipitation, radiation, snow and soil moisture, with an uncertainty estimate from a 10-member ensemble at three-hourly intervals and pre-computed monthly means. ECMWF produces it for the Copernicus Climate Change Service; it replaced ERA-Interim. Coverage is global from 1940 to the present, updated daily with a latency of a few days, regridded to 0.25 degrees for the reanalysis (0.5 degrees for ocean waves and the ensemble). Data are accessible from the Climate Data Store through web forms and an API, with subsets on single levels and pressure levels, under a CC BY 4.0 licence at no cost after free registration. Caveats: early decades rest on far fewer observations, preliminary ERA5T data can be revised, and grid-scale values smooth local extremes. It is the common weather and climate forcing for hazard exposure, heat and wind stress on infrastructure, renewable resource and demand modelling; related records are GloFAS, ISIMIP, the CMIP6 projections and the NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 downscaled data.
